chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Most of the deficiency of intelligence occurs due to the flash of greed.

key_terms.بُرُوقِ: Flashes of lightning, metaphorically describing the sudden, dazzling, and blinding nature of desires.
key_terms.مَصَارِعِ: Plural of masri', meaning places of falling, defeat, or deficiency; here referring to the downfall or lack of intellect.

ai.seo_question: What is the main cause of intellectual deficiency according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this aphorism from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employs the metaphor of 'buruq' (flashes of lightning) to illustrate how the intense, dazzling nature of worldly desires temporarily blinds the intellect, causing it to stumble. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding that greed (shahwah) acts as a veil (hijab) over the heart, obscuring divine truth and leading to spiritual and rational deficiency. The saying underscores the practical need for self-discipline to maintain clarity of mind amidst the fleeting allure of material pursuits.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 219. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
Most of the deficiency of intelligence occurs due to the flash of greed. [1]
